courses.courseDescription: EFL 510 equips prospective teachers of English as a Foreign Language with the advanced knowledge and practical competencies required to integrate artificial intelligence and emerging digital technologies into contemporary language classrooms, highlighting the benefits, limitations, and ethical considerations of incorporating both digital technologies and AI-enhanced tools in the language classroom. Building on core concepts in ICT and e-learning, the course familiarizes students with essential terminology, foundational computer skills for educators, and the effective use of digital platforms such as wikis, blogs, podcasts, and learning-management environments. In addition to these established tools, the course places strong emphasis on the pedagogical potential of AI, including generative AI systems, adaptive learning platforms, automated assessment tools, intelligent tutoring systems, and data-driven learneranalytics. It aims to equip students with practical and theoretical knowledge of artificial intelligence applications in language teaching. This ensures graduates are prepared to integrate emerging technologies into classroom practice and remain current with innovations in TEFL pedagogy. Through guided practice and critical reflection, MA students explore how AI can be used to enhance lesson design, personalize instruction, support multilingual learners, foster collaborative learning, and streamline classroom management tasks. Students also develop advanced online search strategies, engage in responsible and ethical e-communication, and learn to design, manage, and evaluate AI-supported e-projects. By the end of the course, participants gain firsthand experience in applying AI technologies to create effective, equitable, and innovative EFL learning environments that reflect current global trends in digital education.
courses.courseObjectives: By the end of the course, students will be able to: • Familiarize student-teachers with current research and theoretical frameworks on the benefits, limitations, and ethical considerations of incorporating both digital technologies and AI-enhanced tools in the language classroom. • Equip students-teachers with practical and theoretical knowledge of artificial intelligence applications in language teaching. • Acquaint students with modern classroom technologies, such as smart/interactive whiteboards, tablets, weblogs, wikis, and learning portals alongside AI-driven applications, including generative AI platforms, adaptive learning systems, intelligent tutoring tools, and automated feedback engines. • Implement teaching methods and evaluation strategies that leverage digital and AI-powered technologies to maximize student learning, promote differentiated instruction, and support evidence-based assessment practices. • Apply knowledge gained to create blogs, e-portfolios, AI-supported multimedia tasks, and other digital artefacts that showcase students’ written and multimodal assignments. • Participate effectively as team members in the design and implementation of collaborative digital projects, such as e-portfolios, weblogs, wikis, and AI-augmented online tasks that develop communication, creativity, and problem-solving skills. • Summarize, evaluate, and repurpose information gathered from the internet and AI-assisted searches as part of integrating digital literacy and responsible use of AI into the curriculum.
courses.courseOutcomes: At the end of the module, learners will be expected to: A1: Demonstrate advanced understanding of the benefits, challenges, and ethical implications of integrating AI and digital technologies in EFL and bilingual learning environments. A2: Demonstrate comprehensive knowledge of ICT, AI systems, generative tools, adaptive platforms, and intelligent tutoring technologies relevant to EFL pedagogy. A3: Explain the role of theoretical frameworks and models for the effective integration of AI, ICT, and blended learning into classroom practices. A4: Explore and synthesize contemporary research on AI-supported EFL, bilingual proficiency, translanguaging tools, and digital ecosystems in education. B1. Critically analyse and evaluate the pedagogical value, limitations, and ethical aspects of AI-powered and digital tools used in language teaching. B2. Conduct advanced online and AI-assisted searches, synthesize digital information, and incorporate findings into lesson plans, projects, and academic writing. B3. Use a range of AI-supported e-learning portals—blogs, wikis, podcasts, adaptive platforms, and bilingual AI tools—for collaborative learning and instructional design. B4. Evaluate the effectiveness, usability, and learner impact of AI-based, ICT-based, and IoT-integrated tools through evidence-based criteria. C1. Identify learners' needs and use this insight to select, adapt, and evaluate AI-supported materials and technologies. C2. Apply up-to-date AI pedagogy, digital methodologies, and technical skills to support effective teaching practices in EFL/bilingual contexts. C3. Practise advanced web searches, e-learning platforms, smart boards, AI tutoring systems, and classroom technologies. C4. Design, implement, and evaluate AI-enhanced lesson plans, bilingual tasks, and technology-rich materials aligned with learners' proficiency and learning goals. D1. Use AI tools, ICT skills, and advanced digital literacy practices across other MA modules and professional contexts. D2. Select, design, and evaluate innovative AI-driven teaching methods, resources, and technological tools applicable across diverse classroom settings. D3. Collaborate effectively with other tutors and colleagues to create AI-enhanced, innovative classroom environments and instructional resources. D4. Conduct advanced academic research skills using AI-assisted methods, digital scholarship tools, and critical evaluation frameworks.

courses.courseDescription: EFL 513 offers an overview of several of the major theoretical and methodological frameworks for doing discourse analysis. It provides opportunity to try out different methods in the analysis of discourse using the different theoretical perspectives and methodologies from linguistic, socio-cultural and cognitive viewpoints. The course enhances students’ understanding of the verbal and nonverbal aspects of language, and allows them to explore the significance of discourse analysis and its related concepts in the study of language.
courses.courseObjectives: • Acquainting students with the ontological and epistemological premises which are embedded in language • Orienting the students with the different approaches to analysing discourse, and the different methods which are used for doing discourse analysis • Introducing the students to the limitations of discourse analysis and how to apply reliability methods when analysing discourse Introducing the notion of Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA) which links discourse to power relations.
courses.courseOutcomes: A1: Explain the scope, significance, and key concepts of discourse analysis and its role in the study of language in use. A2: Describe major theoretical concepts in discourse analysis, as they relate to linguistic meaning and social practice. A3: Explain key methodological challenges, limitations, and reliability concerns in discourse analysis. B1: Critically analyse discourse data by selecting appropriate analytical approaches and frameworks in relation to research aims and context B2: Critically evaluate different discourse-analytic methods and approaches, considering their theoretical assumptions, strengths, and limitations. B3: Critically interpret strategies used to ensure reliability and validity in discourse analysis, including triangulation and complementary analytical methods. B4: Critically evaluate the relationship between discourse, ideology, and power in social, institutional, media, and educational contexts. C1: Conduct systematic discourse analyses by selecting appropriate data, applying relevant analytical frameworks, and linking textual findings to their social, cultural, or political contexts. C2: Apply practical methods to avoid analysis bias such as inter and intra-reliability methods, and triangulation of data analysis C3: Apply principles of discourse analysis, including Critical Discourse Analysis, to interpret and evaluate language use in educational contexts, with particular reference to EFL classroom interaction and materials D1: Present discourse data clearly and coherently in written and oral academic formats, using appropriate disciplinary conventions. D2: Select and justify suitable analytical approaches and methods for objective discourse analysis, demonstrating methodological awareness and rigour. D3: Critically interpret links between discourse, ideology, and power in social and institutional contexts, communicating informed perspectives. D4: Adapt discourse-analytic knowledge and skills to EFL classroom interaction, teaching materials, and other applied language contexts

courses.courseDescription: EFL 501 introduces major theories of language learning, including behaviourism, cognitivism, innatism (e.g., Universal Grammar), and interactionist perspectives. For each theoretical framework, students become familiar with its core tenets, pedagogical implications, and classroom applications. The module highlights how behaviourist, cognitivist, and innatist perspectives shape teaching practices and redefine the teacher’s role as a facilitator of learning and designer of meaningful communicative environments. The module links closely with other programme components by emphasising the importance of language theories in informing classroom practices and theory-driven pedagogical decisions. Students learn to evaluate how factors such as proficiency level, sociocultural context, and learning needs inform lesson planning and the informed selection of teaching methods. This prepares students for subsequent modules in methodology, AI technology in the classroom, and practicum, where theory-informed, context-sensitive instructional decisions are essential.
courses.courseObjectives: Familiarize students with the major theories of language learning. Engage students with the activities that represent each of the main theories of language learning. Introduce students to the differences between the major theories of language learning. Introduce students to the two major schools of linguistic thought: structuralism and generativism, and their role in the teaching-learning practice, together with other learning models.
courses.courseOutcomes: At the end of the module, learners will be expected to: A1: Explain the key principles, assumptions, and teaching implications of major language learning theories. A2: Summarise and interpret key research findings in Language Learning Using Recent Educational Technology Studies. A3 : Describe and justify the teacher's role as a learning facilitator through relating theoretical perspectives to theory and classroom practices. B1: Differentiate major language learning theories by comparing their assumptions and key features. B2: Relate teaching and learning strategies to each theoretical framework across different learning contexts. B3: Synthesize elements from different language-learning theories by identifying where they converge and complement each other. C1: Critically analyse the major characteristics of each language learning model. C2: Critically examine language learning theories to identify and justify effective strategies for cooperative and interactive classroom contexts. C3: Apply evaluative discourse analysis to assess language use in authentic professional and communicative contexts. D1: Communicate ideas pertinent to language learning theories clearly and coherently in spoken and written academic contexts. D2: Apply interpersonal and teamwork skills to collaborate effectively with others in group discussions and cooperative tasks. D3: Reflect on and evaluate skills, identifying strengths and areas for growth, and applying them in new contexts

courses.courseDescription: EFL 502 aims to equip prospective teachers and researchers of English with a comprehensive understanding of the principles, approaches, and types of research methods required for conducting rigorous research at Master’s level. The module introduces students to a range of qualitative, quantitative, and mixed-methods research designs commonly used in English language teaching and learning, and develops their ability to critically evaluate published research in international contexts. In line with international MA TEFL standards, the module addresses key theoretical, practical, and ethical considerations in foreign language research, including research integrity, academic honesty, and responsible data management. It also integrates the informed and ethical use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in educational research, such as literature review support, data analysis, and academic writing, with a strong emphasis on critical engagement, transparency, and ethical practice.
courses.courseObjectives: Prepare graduate students in research methods to be able to critically evaluate published research and design their own research projects. Introduce students to the main research methods that they can use to conduct small-scale research in the foreign language classroom, including case study method, quasi-experimental method, qualitative experiment, meta-analysis, descriptive research, action research, error analysis, research and development (R&D), and survey method. Offer learners insight into the principles for undertaking research. Provide hands-on experience in research design. Provide instruments for data collection. Provide ways of evaluating published research. Provide techniques of report writing. Integrate the informed, critical, and ethical use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support literature review, research design, data analysis, and academic writing, with a strong emphasis on academic integrity, transparency, and responsible use.
courses.courseOutcomes: A. Knowledge and understanding At the end of the module, learners should be able to: A1 . Review small-scale research, demonstrating an understanding of the research methods literature A2 . Demonstrate understanding of how technology, including AI tools, supports EFL research processes while observing ethical and academic integrity standards. A3 . Evaluate the suitability of data collection and analysis methods for small-scale research. A4 . Critically reflect on the process of carrying out research and on the development of research competence. B. Cognitive skills At the end of the module, learners should be able to: B1 . Analyse and interpret core research methods and theoretical ideas in the designated field. B2 . Critically evaluate the suitability of research methods for EFL topics, including appropriate use of technology and AI. B3 . Provide a rationale for small-scale research design with reference to methodology, ethics, and responsible use of digital and AI tools. C. Practical and professional skills At the end of the module, learners should be able to: C1. Use ICT and digital research tools, including appropriate AI applications, to support academic research in line with ethical standards. C2 . Design a small-scale research project demonstrating effective methods, data collection, and responsible use of digital and AI tools. C3 . Produce clear, well-structured research reports that follow academic conventions and transparently acknowledge digital and AI tool use. D. Key transferable skills At the end of the module, learners should be able to: D1 . Manage research independently, demonstrating effective time management and responsible use of digital and AI tools. D2 . Apply academic and digital literacies in structured presentations and effective information processing. D3 . Critically evaluate and communicate academic and professional information using appropriate discourse conventions. D4 . Use autonomy and enhanced meta-cognitive strategies with regard to study skills and further professional development.

courses.courseDescription: EFL 506 is designed to equip pre-service teachers with effective classroom management and instructional strategies for English language learning environments. The course integrates theory and practice to develop management skills applicable to TEFL classrooms. Through a focus on core management principles and evidence-based procedures, the course prepares future teachers to create safe, supportive, and productive learning environments that promote student engagement and effective language learning.
courses.courseObjectives: Attain organizational strategies Establish rules and procedures Manage student work Establish a positive climate for learning Plan and conduct instruction to prevent management problems Communicate effectively with students Use observational techniques and functional behaviour assessment techniques to analyze behaviour problems and determine appropriate interventions Implement classroom problem solving meetings to address problems Manage crisis situations in the classroom and school
courses.courseOutcomes: A. Knowledge and understanding By the end of this module, students should be able to: A1. Illustrate key theories and techniques of classroom management and pedagogical purposes A2. Classify the technical, linguistic, behavioural, and intellectual principles underpinning effective classroom management. A3. Identify classroom management practices and approaches related to physical setting, resource use, time allocation, learner engagement, and content organisation. B. Cognitive skills B1. Analyse appropriate classroom management practices for a given teaching context based on learners' needs, lesson objectives, and classroom constraints. B2. Design innovative tasks for course content by adapting materials to learners' profiles and instructional goals. B3. Observe, interpret, and document students' behaviour to match an appropriate intervention strategy to vary class activities (or setting) in the desired direction C. Practical and professional skills By the end of this module, students should be able to: C1. Plan and organise instructional resources to support learning effectively. C2. Design classroom layouts and procedures to ensure safe, efficient, and positive learning environments. C3. Develop time-management plans that integrate content, strategies, grouping, and learner engagement. C4. Identify and adapt instructional strategies to address diverse learning styles. C5. Apply affective domain models to manage classroom atmosphere, motivation, and student wellbeing. C6. Role-play effective and ineffective teaching behaviours as related to classroom management. D Key transferable skills By the end of this module, students should be able to: D1. Apply effective classroom management strategies by organising learning activities, managing learner behaviour, and maintaining a productive learning environment. D2: Adapt to different teaching environments by modifying instructional strategies, classroom routines, and communication approaches to suit varied educational contexts.

courses.courseDescription: EFL 507 aims to acquaint students with the most recent trends, methods, and procedures in the field of language testing and assessment. The course provides students with a solid understanding of theoretical and practical issues related to test design, development, and evaluation. In addition, students will become familiar with a wide variety of test types used to assess both receptive and productive language skills, enabling them to apply appropriate testing and assessment techniques in educational and professional contexts.
courses.courseObjectives: To familiarize candidates with the vital role of testing in foreign language learning classrooms. To provide adequate insight into the close and inseparable relationship between teaching and testing in EFL contexts, with attention to how AI can support instructional and assessment practices. To train candidates in the principles and practical procedures involved in assessing learners' communicative competence. To raise candidates' awareness of the distinctions among measurement, assessment, and evaluation in language testing. To develop an understanding of the challenges and limitations that may hinder effective language testing, including ethical and practical concerns related to the use of AI. To equip learners with the skills needed to design and construct essay-type and multiple-choice test items, as well as to utilize AI tools to support test development and analysis.
courses.courseOutcomes: A. Knowledge and understanding Upon the completion of this module, students should be able to: A1: Demonstrate knowledge of contemporary ideas, principles, and approaches to language testing. A2: Explain and relate current language testing methods to recent theories of language learning. A3: Exemplify the principles of classroom test construction and evaluation by outlining test formats, types, and criteria. A4: Explain the use of tests in research by evaluating test items and addressing ethical considerations. B. Cognitive skills B1: Analyse issues of accountability and fairness in language testing. B2: Critically interpret the professional concerns of language test developers by considering constraints, ethics, and quality standards in test design. B3: Differentiate validity and reliability through analysis of test examples and their implications for test quality and decision-making. C. Practical and professional skills C1: Design, apply, and score assessment tasks for productive language skills (writing and speaking) by using appropriate criteria, rating scales, and feedback procedures. C2: Select, administer, and evaluate assessment instruments for receptive language skills (listening and reading) by analysing tasks and learners' performance. C3: Apply and justify standardised criteria to assess essays in TEFL and related fields by providing consistent scoring and constructive, criterion-referenced feedback. D Key transferable skills By the end of the module, learners should be able to: D1: Construct clear and effective multiple-choice. D2: Formulate well-designed short-answer questions aligned with targeted cognitive and linguistic skills. D3: Compare question types by evaluating their strengths, limitations, and suitability for specific assessment purposes. D4: Review and revise test items systematically by applying established evaluation criteria.

courses.courseDescription: EFL 508 introduces potential tutors to an integrated approach in planning and executing successful teaching sessions. The first half of the semester is devoted to classroom observation, microteaching activities, and the development of lesson plans. The second half of the semester focuses on hands-on experience through observing teachers in a live classroom context (e.g., the English Language Unit - AOU Foundation Programme) and engaging in teaching one or more sessions in the presence of both the session teacher and the EFL module supervisor. Students are also engaged in preparing reflective reports on these experiences to support professional growth and self-evaluation. Learners, specifically inexperienced candidates, have the opportunity to participate more in in-field assignments, leading to professional development. Familiarity with course material in teaching grammar, pronunciation, and vocabulary, which reflects language teaching awareness, is combined with other necessary skills such as professional conduct, methods of instruction, time management, needs assessment, and proficiency testing. The module provides an opportunity to experience the practical aspects of EFL after being coached in the theoretical components.
courses.courseObjectives: The module aims at: • Helping potential tutors develop the practical skills necessary for analysing and evaluating effective teaching in the EFL classroom. • Applying appropriate instructional methodologies to teach grammar, pronunciation, and vocabulary. • Guiding potential tutors in designing and conducting needs assessments, placement measures and proficiency tests as necessary. • Familiarising potential tutors with the means of planning effective lessons, facilitating and evaluating classroom instruction, especially through the use of modern computer technology. • Helping potential tutors evaluate their own teaching in order to improve their skills as classroom instructors, based on feedback from mentor and self-evaluation. • Engaging potential tutors in instructional and reflective practices to develop effective teaching
courses.courseOutcomes: At the end of the module, learners will be expected to: A1: Explain the objectives, structure, and professional requirements of a teaching practicum in a TEFL context. A2: Describe key principles underlying the design and implementation of lesson plans for TEFL classrooms. A3: Explain the roles and responsibilities of teachers in facilitating effective learning in TEFL settings. A4 : Identify core concepts and models of reflective teaching practice in EFL A5 : Describe fundamental principles and types of assessment used in TEFL, including their purposes and applications. B1 : Analyse learners' needs, contextual factors, and learning objectives in order to select and justify appropriate teaching strategies in TEFL classrooms. B2 : Analytically explain the requirements for pre-session, in-session and post session tasks B3 : Discuss lesson plans and classroom activities designed to develop listening, comprehension, pronunciation, classroom interaction, and drill-based practice. B4 : Critically evaluate teaching practices and methodological choices through the application of reflective frameworks, proposing evidence-based alternative approaches where appropriate. B5: Analyse critically the effectiveness of different types of assessment in TEFL in relation to learning outcomes, learner needs, and instructional goals. C1: Demonstrate professional conduct: authority, language, appearance and attitude. C2: Adopt and apply suitable foreign language teaching strategies in actual classroom. C3. Plan, and deliver TEFL lessons through reflective professional practice, drawing on mentor feedback, peer observation, and self-evaluation. D1: Communicate with confidence and clarity on professional issues related to TEFL, using appropriate academic and professional discourse D2: Demonstrate skills on working co-operatively with others in planning, delivering, and evaluating TEFL instruction. D3: Demonstrate enhanced self-awareness and professional confidence by reflecting on their own skills and identifying ways these skills can be transferred to new teaching and professional contexts.

courses.courseTitle: English Language Teaching Methods – Receptive and Productive Skills
courses.courseDescription: EFL509 covers practical and valid approaches and techniques needed to teach English language receptive and productive skills. The module prepares students to teach receptive skills (listening and reading) as well as productive skills (speaking and writing) needed to pursue their career as ESL/EFL teachers. In this module, students learn to examine the challenges facing methodologists, material designers, and developers as well as foreign language teachers in analysing and choosing the suitable approaches, methods and materials for use in English language classes. The general aim of this module is to equip students with the theoretical foundations, methodological principles, and classroom techniques necessary to design and deliver effective English language instruction that integrates critical thinking, communicative competence, and evidence-based pedagogical approaches. Drawing on contemporary ELT research and established teaching frameworks, the module seeks to develop reflective practitioners capable of selecting, adapting, and evaluating instructional strategies that foster language development, learner autonomy, and higher order thinking skills in diverse ESL/EFL contexts. By the end of the course, the students should be able to understand the general principles of teaching receptive and productive skills and evaluate teaching and learning materials as used in classes of small and large numbers of learners.
courses.courseObjectives: The module aims to provide the learners with necessary skills through: Promoting students' knowledge of the different methods of teaching receptive and productive skills in English as a foreign language. Examining the different approaches and views on the nature of the receptive and productive skills and how these views are applied to reading, listening, speaking and writing programs, materials and classroom tasks. Integrating critical thinking strategies into the teaching of receptive and productive skills by enabling students to design tasks that promote analysis, inference, evaluation, and learner engagement with authentic texts. Encouraging reflective teaching practices by guiding students to evaluate, adapt, and justify instructional decisions based on established ELT principles, learner needs, and context-sensitive pedagogical frameworks. Guiding the students to adopt and effectively practice approaches of teaching new vocabulary items, generating ideas and expanding them. Promoting the students' knowledge of the uses of computers in language learning and teaching in light of Computer Assisted Language Learning (CALL). Developing a lesson plan on the basis of the learnt methods of teaching receptive and productive skills. Using interactive programs to promote learner autonomy of learning how to teach receptive and productive skills. Improving students' language proficiency and their ability to produce and convey meaning through well-structured utterances.
courses.courseOutcomes: At the end of the module, learners will be expected to: A1. Identify the historical development of methods and approaches in the teaching of English (receptive and productive skills). A2. Distinguish varied methods of organizing instruction (bottom-up and top-down). A3. Recognize the current curriculum as a framework for professional development, including implementation of educational technology. A4. Identify the tones of the English sound system and varieties of English and demonstrate awareness of various cultural contexts and different methods of communicating in English. A5: Recognize the grammatical structure of English and how meaning, vocabulary, speaking, and mechanics of writing can be developed B1. Identify the core components of receptive and productive language abilities, including – listening and reading processes, – speaking and writing abilities, and – vocabulary knowledge. B2. Demonstrate understanding of bottom-up and top-down approaches in developing receptive and productive language skills. B3. Apply inductive and deductive approaches to develop learners' reading, speaking, and writing skills through real-life contexts. B4. Facilitate differentiated activities that develop receptive and productive skills, including effective use of digital tools. C1. Design, deliver, and assess EFL lessons integrating listening, reading, speaking, and writing while addressing learners' diverse needs and proficiency levels. C2. Use updated, effective methods to teach listening, reading, speaking, and writing with appropriate techniques, materials, and assessments. C3. Reflect on and critically assess teaching practices in relation to current EFL curricula and learning outcomes, making informed adjustments to improve student learning. C4. Collaborate and work independently on EFL teaching issues, demonstrating professional responsibility, reflective practice, and ongoing development. C5. Effectively use digital tools, online resources, and computer applications to enhance the teaching and learning of listening, reading, speaking, and writing. D1. Apply reflective practice to evaluate learning and professional actions within ethical and institutional frameworks. D2. Work independently and collaboratively to analyse and solve learning-related problems. D3. Apply current approaches to developing receptive and productive skills. D4. Select and apply strategies to develop receptive and productive skills, including effective use of digital tools.

courses.courseDescription: This elective course in linguistics and its applications offers essential knowledge and resources for students pursuing an MA in Teaching English as a Foreign Language (TEFL). It equips future teachers with a solid understanding of language structure and use, which supports their exploration of TEFL theories, development of effective teaching methodologies, and enhancement of professional teaching skills.
courses.courseObjectives: This module aims at: -Providing students with a solid theoretical foundation in linguistics and the English language. -Giving students sufficient information on the various branches of English linguistics. -Describing the structure of English and compare it to the structure of other languages; -Introducing students to linguistic applications, especially psycholinguistics and TEFL. -Providing details pertaining to the difficulties which hinder the achievement of the previous aims.
courses.courseOutcomes: At the end of the module, learners will be expected to: A1: Explain the nature, functions, and key characteristics of human language, drawing on established linguistic frameworks. A2. Describe the core principles and systems of English phonetics and phonology, including their relevance to language description and use. A3. Identify the fundamental systems of English morphology and syntax and their role in structuring meaning in spoken and written discourse. A4. Define the major concepts and systems of English semantics and pragmatics, including the interaction between meaning, context, and language use. B1: Analyse linguistic concepts and frameworks in order to explain how insights from language study can be applied to language teaching and learning contexts. B2: Compare major theories of first language acquisition, identifying key stages, processes, and influencing factors. B3: Evaluate theories of second and foreign language acquisition in relation to adult learners and TEFL contexts. C1: Apply principles of English phonetics and phonology to analyse spoken language data. C2: Use analytical techniques from English morphology and syntax to examine and explain linguistic structures in authentic written and spoken texts. C3: Implement concepts from semantics and pragmatics to analyse meaning, context, and language use, with reference to real-life communicative situations and pedagogical examples. D1: Communicate complex linguistic concepts and analyses clearly and coherently in spoken and written academic contexts. D2: Engage constructively in academic discussion and collaborative tasks by presenting informed viewpoints and responding critically to the ideas of others. D3: Adapt knowledge of linguistic concepts and analytical approaches to new contexts relevant to TEFL, applied linguistics, and further academic study.

courses.courseDescription: The course offers a conception of grammar that takes into account the needs of EFL learners. In contrast with prescriptive or descriptive grammars, pedagogic grammars in TEFL contexts include basic and frequently used structures chosen for their maximum relevance to students who plan to use English for ordinary purposes, especially academic study. The module incorporates AI-supported grammar instruction and corpus-based approaches, enabling learners to explore innovative methods for analysing and teaching grammar in digital environments.
courses.courseObjectives: Pedagogic Grammar aims at: Teaching form, meaning and use of Grammar in context, making sure that learners are able to use grammar accurately and appropriately. . Allowing candidates to manipulate sentences for free production. Permitting the categorisation of grammar (form, meaning, use) into units which will form a syllabus or teaching objectives. Allowing consideration of how far a conscious focus on grammar rules assists in EFL acquisition. Developing the ability to integrate AI and corpus-based tools into grammar teaching and analysis.
courses.courseOutcomes: At the end of the module, learners will be expected to: A1: Explain the key components and principles of pedagogic grammar, including the relationship between grammatical form, meaning, and use in EFL contexts. A2: Explain the pedagogical value of pedagogic grammar compared to prescriptive and descriptive models. A3: Describe the key differences between pedagogic grammar and other grammatical frameworks, with reference to their purposes, scope, and relevance for EFL learning and teaching. At the end of the module learners will be expected to: B1: Analyse grammatical form–meaning–use relationships in spoken and written English in order to explain how grammatical choices shape meaning in context. B2: Analyse spoken and written English texts to identify grammatical patterns relevant to pedagogic grammar using corpus-based and AI-supported tools. B3: Critically evaluate different interpretations of grammatical structures, considering alternative analyses and learner-related factors. B4: Critically analyse the role of visual, spatial, and contextual cues in supporting learners’ understanding of grammatical meaning and use. C1: Apply knowledge of English grammatical phenomena to analyse authentic spoken and written texts using appropriate grammatical metalanguage. C2: Select and apply different approaches to grammatical description (including corpus-based and AI-supported approaches) in order to explain grammatical form, meaning, and use for pedagogic purposes. C3: Apply principles of pedagogic grammar to support learners' understanding and use of grammatical structures in EFL contexts. C4: Use appropriate grammatical metalanguage accurately and consistently when describing and discussing grammatical features. D1: Perform an analysis of a previously unknown grammatical phenomenon. D2: Show familiarity with the dynamic context in which grammar writing and teaching takes place. D3: Develop strategies for approaching grammar in the classroom (including AI-enhanced and technology-supported approaches).

courses.courseDescription: This course aims to introduce students to the fundamental notions of contemporary phonetics and phonology. EFL515 starts with a survey of the basic notions of articulatory phonetics, with special emphasis on the standard pronunciation varieties of British and American English (RP and Gen Am E, respectively). This is followed by an overview of supra-segmental features, such as stress, connected speech and intonation, assimilation, as well as international variants of English (World Englishes). Students will also be familiarized with the basic tenets of generative phonology, which are illustrated primarily with reference to English examples. Students will be taught to formulate the most important rules of lexical and post-lexical phonology of English. In addition, students shall be trained to use effective techniques and activities when teaching pronunciation. This module is significant as it refines students’ pronunciation skills and provides them with important background in the fundamental aspects of phonetics and phonology. The module is connected with many modules in the programme including EFL503N: English Language Teaching Methods, in which students are trained on how to teach receptive and productive skills, i.e., listening, speaking, reading and writing.
courses.courseObjectives: This module aims at Familiarizing students with how to approach English pronunciation descriptively. Guiding students to develop and master the basic notions and terms of phonological and phonetic description. Enabling students to apply their knowledge of English phonetics and phonology to improve their own pronunciation in further studies of languages and linguistics and in teaching. Assisting students in explaining the basic functions of English intonation.
courses.courseOutcomes: At the end of this module, learners should be able to: A1: Explain the principles of speech production, including the role of the organs of speech and articulatory mechanisms involved in the production of English sounds. A2: Distinguish key patterns of phonetic and phonological variation in English, including differences across major accent varieties and contexts of use. A3: Recognize how segmental and suprasegmental features of English (e.g., phonemes, stress, rhythm, intonation) contribute to meaning in spoken communication. A4: Describe the fundamental features of English phonological systems, including phonemes, allophones, phonological processes, and basic rule-based representations. B1: Analyse the manner and place of articulation of English consonants and vowels using established phonetic classification systems. B2: Critically classify English vowel and consonant sounds according to their articulatory and acoustic properties. B3: Examine phonological processes operating in connected English speech, including assimilation, elision, linking, and stress placement. B4 . Compare major accent varieties of English (e.g. Received Pronunciation and General American), identifying systematic phonetic and phonological differences. C1: Apply phonetic and phonological principles to produce and interpret phonetic and phonemic transcriptions of English sounds in isolation and in connected speech C2: Produce English stress, rhythm, and intonation patterns accurately in spoken language using appropriate phonetic conventions. C3 : Diagnose common pronunciation difficulties experienced by EFL learners by relating them to phonetic, phonological, and cross-linguistic factors. C4 . Apply phonetic and phonological knowledge to select and justify appropriate techniques and activities for teaching English pronunciation in EFL contexts. 1: Communicate phonetic and phonological concepts accurately and coherently in spoken and written academic English, using appropriate technical terminology. D2: Apply effective listening and analytical skills to identify pronunciation features and problems in spoken English across different contexts D3: Select and use appropriate instructional techniques and resources to support the teaching and learning of English pronunciation in EFL contexts. D4. Use digital and audio-based tools appropriately for phonetic analysis, pronunciation practice, and independent learning.

courses.courseDescription: This module aims to introduce students to the major areas of semantics and pragmatics and their relation to the domain of foreign language acquisition. Semantic topics covered in the module include lexical meaning, word coinage, multi-word units, collocations, denotations, connotations, etc. Pragmatic topics include Grice’s maxims of the cooperative principle, flouting maxims, politeness strategies, conversational implicatures, speech acts, etc. This module is significant as it provides learners with an important background in the areas of semantics and pragmatics relevant to the domain of EFL learning and teaching.
courses.courseObjectives: Introducing students to theories of meaning and theories of language use Providing students with a sound foundation in semantics and pragmatics Discussing various aspects necessary to comprehend the denotative and connotative meaning of a lexical item, a collocation, an idiom, a multi-word expression, etc. Familiarizing students with cases where cultural norms are observed and where they are flouted. Showing students how communication strategies can differ from one culture to another.
courses.courseOutcomes: A1: Explain the basic tenets of semantics and pragmatics. A2: Identify major concepts in semantics and pragmatics, such as conversational norms, and how these may vary across cultures. A3: Distinguish different methods of coining words and analysing meaning at the word level and beyond. Distinguish different methods of word coinage and approaches to analysing meaning at the word level and beyond. A4: Explain cross-cultural norms and the operation of Gricean Maxims.B1: Analyse meaning in language by examining how semantic and pragmatic principles operate in EFL teaching and learning contexts, including spoken and written classroom discourse. B1: Analyse meaning in language by examining how semantic and pragmatic principles operate in EFL teaching and learning contexts, including spoken and written classroom discourse. B2: Interpret language use in EFL contexts, taking into account speaker intention, inference, and shared knowledge in teacher–learner and learner–learner interaction. B3: Analyze linguistic texts showing how semantic and pragmatic features contribute to meaning creation. C1: Apply key concepts from semantics and pragmatics to interpret meaning in spoken and written texts used in EFL teaching and learning contexts. C2: Apply concepts from semantics and pragmatics to support the teaching of meaning and language use in EFL contexts, including explaining pragmatic phenomena to learners in accessible ways. C3: Demonstrate ability to judge appropriate use of language in light of the semantic and pragmatic norms. C4: Apply semantic and pragmatic principles to identify and explain sources of misunderstanding or ambiguity encountered by EFL learners. D1: Communicate semantic and pragmatic concepts clearly and accurately in spoken and written academic English, using appropriate linguistic terminology. D2: Explain the role played by semantics and pragmatics in teaching and learning a foreign language. D3: Conduct text-analysis research that illustrates the impact of semantics and pragmatics in manipulating meaning. D4. Use digital and online resources effectively to support independent learning and professional development in semantics, pragmatics, and TEFL.

courses.courseDescription: EFL522 offers an overview of several of the major theoretical and methodological frames on critical linguistics and error analysis for students intending to teach English as a foreign language. The course explores the role of interference and language transfer mechanism. In addition, the course offers description of the formal distinctions between the learners' first and second languages to predict errors. The course aims to frame error analysis approaches within CL in order to relate hypotheses to empirical testing in TEFL preparation.
courses.courseObjectives: Introducing students to theories of Contrastive Linguistics (CL) and Error Analysis (EA). Familiarizing students with the general theories of Contrastive Analysis (CA), patterns of contrast (phonology, morphology, syntax and semantics) and application of the results of CA to teaching a foreign language. Acquainting students with the theories related to Error Analysis (EA) at the levels of phonology, morphology, syntax and semantics, and their practical application in teaching a foreign language. Guiding students on the symmetries and asymmetries between English and Arabic.
courses.courseOutcomes: At the end of the module, learners will be expected to: A1: Explain the major principles and theoretical foundations of contrastive linguistics and error analysis. A2: Recognise the role of contrastive linguistics in the field of teaching English as a foreign language, particularly in relation to language transfer and interference. A3: Discuss how error analysis contributes to the identification, interpretation, and understanding of EFL learners' errors. A4. Describe key areas of contrast between English and Arabic at the levels of phonology, morphology, syntax, and semantics, and their relevance to EFL learning. B1: Show understanding of the major theories of Contrastive Linguistics and Error Analysis. B2: Demonstrate competence in conducting basic research tasks in Contrastive Linguistics and Error Analysis. B3: Evaluate different approaches to Contrastive Linguistics and Error Analysis and how these approaches can be applied in EFL teaching. B4. Interpret errors produced by EFL learners using principles of contrastive linguistics and error analysis. C1: Conduct contrastive analysis of texts in Arabic and English. C2: Use error analysis approaches in detecting EFL learners' language problems. C3: Carry out research in the EFL field using contrastive linguistics and error analysis knowledge D1. Communicate ideas related to contrastive linguistics and error analysis in spoken and written academic English, based on research and independent investigation. D2. Apply analytical thinking skills to examine linguistic data and learner errors in EFL contexts. D3. Reflect on awareness of cross-linguistic differences and their impact on EFL learning and teaching. D4. Adapt relevant academic and digital resources effectively to support independent learning and professional development in TEFL.

courses.preRequisite: Completion of 32 credits from the compulsory modules
courses.courseDescription: This course is designed to equip students with the skills needed to develop and structure a research proposal on a topic of their choice. Students will receive guidance in planning, designing, and organizing their proposals while beginning to review relevant literature, applying the knowledge gained in the Research Methods Module (EFL502). The course also emphasizes the responsible and ethical use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support literature searches, reference management, initial data exploration, and drafting, helping students integrate technology effectively into the research planning process.
courses.courseObjectives: The Course Aims at: Providing MA in TEFL students with foundation in the skills and knowledge required to effectively create MA proposals. Supporting MA in TEFL students in developing the research design, writing and sectionalizing the content of their MA proposal. Emphasizing best practices in management, presentation, research skills and ethics necessary to manage proposal efforts. Providing students with practical experience in quantitative research methods, enabling them to use online SPSS for statistical analysis and to interpret results effectively in relation to their research proposals. Developing students' understanding of ethical research practices and responsible use of AI tools for literature review, data organization, and drafting, while fostering critical awareness of AI's methodological and ethical implications.
courses.courseOutcomes: At the end of the module, learners will be expected to: A1. Explain the key components, structure, and conventions of a postgraduate research proposal in TEFL, including topic justification, literature review, research questions, and methodology. A2 . Describe the principles underpinning quantitative and qualitative research methods in TEFL, including the use of statistical analysis tools such as online SPSS. A3 . Summarise core statistical concepts and outputs (descriptive and inferential statistics) relevant to research design and decision-making in TEFL studies. A4. Explain principles of ethical research practice in TEFL, including academic integrity, data management, and the responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in literature searching, data organisation, and drafting. A5. Reflect on the methodological and ethical implications of integrating AI and statistical tools into the research planning and data interpretation processes. B1 : Critically identify and justify a viable research area in TEFL by analysing current literature, research trends, and gaps, including the informed use of AI-supported tools . B1 : Critically identify and justify a viable research area in TEFL by analysing current literature, research trends, and gaps, including the informed use of AI-supported tools. C1. Write a clear, coherent, and academically rigorous MA research proposal in TEFL that demonstrates originality, methodological coherence, and ethical awareness, including the responsible use of AI tools to support drafting and organisation. C2. Present and defend a research proposal orally, clearly justifying the research rationale, methodological choices, statistical approaches, and the use of AI-supported research strategies. C3. Apply appropriate research methods to address a defined TEFL research problem, integrating quantitative techniques At the end of the module, learners will be expected to: (including SPSS where relevant) and qualitative approaches in alignment with research objectives. C4. Use AI and digital research tools effectively and ethically to enhance professional research practice, including literature management, data organisation, preliminary analysis, and presentation of research plans. D1. Transform a broad topic/idea into a proper, feasible research proposal; using AI-supported tools to explore literature, identify research gaps, and organise ideas efficiently. D2. Plan and manage an independent research proposal that adheres to recognised standards of academic writing and research ethics, incorporating suitable quantitative and qualitative approaches where relevant. D3. Carry out systematic library search in scientific and other databases; using digital and AI-assisted tools to retrieve, organise, and manage relevant academic sources D4. Select and critique relevant research; D5. Manage time and meet deadlines. D6. Demonstrate independent learning and professional development skills by reflecting on feedback and responsibly integrating AI and other digital technologies into academic research practice.

courses.courseDescription: This MA dissertation (12,000-16,000 words) is the culmination of the MA in TEFL. It gives students a chance to demonstrate what they have learned throughout the program via writing a piece of research on a TEFL topic. The research should reflect a sound methodology, a robust review of related literature and a well-developed discussion.
courses.courseObjectives: This module aims to provide students with training and knowledge in: working independently on a research project; learning the techniques of postgraduate studies in the humanities; acquiring a range of research tools and methods appropriate to postgraduate studies in the humanities; using physical and online research libraries, their archives and their contents efficiently; using specialist online databases and other online facilities for postgraduate studies. exploring and consolidating what was learnt in the courses. It also aims to teach students to: evaluate critically current research in TEFL; evaluate and critique some of the methods used in humanities research; evaluate bodies of evidence and draw conclusions from them; form arguments at postgraduate level and express those arguments in substantial pieces of writing using proper academic conventions; use feedback from tutors and fellow students effectively to modify this programme of work. be resourceful, clear, concise, efficient, organised and analytical.
courses.courseOutcomes: A1: Explain the selection of appropriate research tools, methods, and approaches for postgraduate research in TEFL. A2: Describe the role and importance of systematic literature review, textual analysis, and bibliographical research in the development of postgraduate TEFL research. A3: Discuss contemporary developments in EFL theory and research to the design, conduct, and interpretation of postgraduate-level TEFL research. A4. Explain ethical principles and research governance requirements relevant to postgraduate research in TEFL, including academic integrity, data management, and responsible use of digital and AI-supported research tools. B1: Engage critically with a range of TEFL/applied linguistics topics and complex critical, theoretical and pedagogic material B2: Contribute in an informed way to current debates on the domain of teaching English as a foreign language. B3: Critically assess the selection and use of research methodologies, methods, and analytical procedures for postgraduate TEFL research, including appropriate use of digital and AI-supported tools. B4: Synthesize and evaluate theoretical and empirical insights to formulate a coherent, independent research argument that contributes to informed debate within the field of TEFL. C1: Compile academic publications relevant to a defined TEFL research topic, using appropriate criteria of quality, relevance, and credibility C2: Critically formulate research-based arguments relevant to TEFL, demonstrating reflexivity and awareness of alternative perspectives. C3: Develop and present a coherent academic argument informed by research and critical engagement with sources. C4: Plan and produce a complete, substantial research work that demonstrates effective research design, appropriate scholarly apparatus, and accurate academic referencing. D1: Plan, manage, and complete an extended independent research project, demonstrating autonomous learning and self-direction. D2: Respond constructively to supervisory and examiner feedback by critically reflecting on and revising academic work. D3: Use information and communication technologies effectively for postgraduate research, including responsible use of AI-based tools. D4: Produce original, well-structured academic work that communicates complex ideas clearly, coherently, and persuasively in accordance with postgraduate conventions.

courses.courseDescription: As an integrated skills syllabus, EL097 combines a general English syllabus with a focus on C21 skills – listening, speaking, reading and writing- together with functions, vocabulary and grammar with 21st century skills such as communication, creativity, critical thinking and study skills in a unique way. The course equips students with essential skills to thrive in the 21st century. The course places extra emphasis on the two language skills of reading and writing through which structure, vocabulary, etc. can be integrated and developed. The course is learner-centered and seeks to introduce thematic topics which aim at developing critical thinking skills. It emphasizes the skill of reading through the application of learning strategies such as prior knowledge, scanning for specific information, skimming for main idea, and getting meaning from context. The course helps students to become more independent learners through extensive reading and writing practice.
courses.courseObjectives: - The module aims to help students to: - Develop their overall communicative ability and become independent, autonomous learners. - Enhance proficiency in listening, speaking, reading, and writing through structured classwork, independent assignments, and online activities. - Read and understand a variety of short texts. - Predict and identify key information in texts. - Develop and increase their vocabulary by encouraging them to use the vocabulary as much as possible so that they can develop an understanding of how the words can be used in various situations. - Enhance their listening skills via practicing listening for gist and listening for specific information. - Develop their speaking skill via engaging in oral practice and taking part in class activities.
courses.courseOutcomes: By the end of the module, learners will be expected to: A1: Gain a basic understanding the four language skills. A2: Develop student’s knowledge and familiarize them with some basic concepts for improving language skills B. Cognitive skills By the end of the module, learners will be expected to: B1: Understand the main ideas and details of conversations, and dialogues on familiar topics such as daily routines, hobbies, and travel. (Listening) B2: Read short texts, such as emails, advertisements, and narratives, to identify key details, infer meaning from context, and summarize the main ideas. C. Practical and professional skills By the end of the module, learners will be expected to: C1: Participate in structured discussions and role-plays, expressing opinions, asking for clarification, and responding to questions using appropriate vocabulary and grammar. C2: Write coherent paragraphs with clear topic sentences, supporting details, and appropriate use of linking words, focusing on topics like personal experiences, jobs in the world, people and places. D Key transferable skills By the end of the module, learners will be expected to: D1: Take notes on essential information from audio recordings, such as instructions, numbers, directions, and use these notes to write brief summaries. D2: Read dialogues, or informational texts aloud with appropriate pronunciation and intonation to improve fluency and confidence in speaking. D3: Use target grammar structures and vocabulary in all four skills (e.g., describing past events, describing daily routines, or giving directions) through a combination of listening, reading, writing, and speaking activities.

courses.courseDescription: As a theme-based, integrated skills course, EL099 continues to develop the four communication skills – listening, speaking reading and writing- together with language functions, vocabulary, and grammar. This allows students to stand on solid ground and gives them the confidence to pursue their study in the university. . Along with the previous modules (EL097 and EL098), it aims to give students a good foundation before attempting more academic reading and writing tasks. It prepares students for EL111 where they will write their first essays and read longer passages.
courses.courseObjectives: 1. Listen to and comprehend varieties of English discourse spoken at normal speed, 2. Speak correctly with good pronunciation, 3. Communicate with ease and confidence on a variety of topics using appropriate structures. 4. Read and understand a variety of English texts of moderate length, complexity, styles and genres, 5. Write different types of paragraphs using appropriate punctuation marks and mechanics of writing.
